Abstract:
This pre-print introduces Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT), a foundational
explanatory system describing invariant, non-moral, non-psychological mechanics governing
human systems across load, detection, identity, power, and time. DHFT is not an application
framework and not a theory-in-progress; it is a closed architectural identification of mechanics
already governing behavior across individual, institutional, and civic scales.
The system is organized around two co-foundational, non-reducible spines: Dimensional
Human Physics (DHP), which defines lawful mechanics of load, constraint, accumulation,
movement, and time; and Dimensional Self Architecture (DSA), which models structural
identity continuity and stabilization over time. A canon-locked bridge domain, Identity
Harmonics, governs lawful coupling between these spines without collapse. A
pre-foundational condition domain specifies when mechanics apply at all, prior to cognition or
interpretation.
DHFT explicitly refuses moral, psychological, intent-based, therapeutic, or regulatory framing.
It distinguishes detection from cognition, authorization from authority, and structural
admissibility from consent. Non-collapse constraints prevent interpretive, applicative, or
narrative backflow into mechanics.
A formal admissibility constraint governing explanatory dependencies is under mathematical
development; at least one declared sub-layer admits explicit dynamical representation while
preserving strict acyclic dependency ordering.
Exposition, derivation, application, and mathematical formalization are intentionally deferred.

Full DHFT Formal System Repository: https://osf.io/9psmd/

Description

Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT) is a formal, non-psychological framework that models stability and collapse in human systems through load, capacity, and boundary dynamics.  It applies across individual, relational, and institutional scales without reliance on narrative or interpretation.

Falsifiability and Failure Conditions

DHFT is falsified only if its governing structural relations fail—specifically, if load under constraint does not produce instability or reorganization, if interpretation alone alters system behavior, if propagation fails under coupling, or if projection violates structural invariance.
DHFT does not model subjective experience (thought, emotion, perception) as variables; dimensionality refers to structural degrees of freedom in system dynamics, not experiential or psychological dimensions.

Within DHFT, Dimensional Human Physics (DHP) defines the lawful structural mechanics of load, capacity, and boundary conditions. Despite its name, “physics” refers to structural mechanics rather than material or biological processes.

DHFT is stewarded by the Somatic Rising Institute, founded by Cara Tonucci. 

Somatic Rising Institute (SRI): 
www.somaticrisinginstitute.org
